intended_object: The universal closure over bound variables: given an infinitary formula φ with n bound-variable slots, the formula ∀x₁…∀xₙ φ with no bound slots left (free variables in α stay free). Inferred from the docstring, which points to the finitary `BoundedFormula.alls` as the model.
explanation:
The definition works by recursion on n. When n = 0 it returns φ unchanged. When n = k+1 it quantifies the last slot with `all`, which leaves a formula with k slots, and recurses. So it applies exactly n universal quantifiers and lands in `FormulaInf ι α`, the type of formulas with no bound-variable slots. This copies Mathlib's finitary `FirstOrder.Language.BoundedFormula.alls` (`| 0, φ => φ | _ + 1, φ => φ.all.alls`), carried over to the infinitary syntax.

Mathlib only has the finitary version, so there is no Mathlib definition of this infinitary object to cite as a counterpart. The definition is also stated at full generality: any language L, any branching type ι, any free-variable type α and any n.
